quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Paying full attention to the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: Work zone signs mean:

options.text: You must stop immediately and back up.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They warn you that construction or maintenance work is happening on or near the road. Drive with extra care in these areas.

questions.question: At night, it is hardest to see:
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than road signs and other objects on the roadside.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a crosswalk.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. You should:

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on the brakes and stop.
Gently apply the brakes to slow down. Then turn the wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brakes to slow down. Then turn the wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, stay calm and gently apply the brakes to slow down. Once at a safe speed, turn the wheel to return to the pavement. Do not jerk the wheel or try to force the vehicle back on the road.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, a pedestrian should walk on the:

options.text: Same side as traffic is moving.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing the traffic they are closest to.

questions.question: If a vehicle with high beams comes toward you, look toward the ____ of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle has high beams on and does not dim them, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: You need extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: The person is a police officer.

questions.explanation: A white cane means the pedestrian is blind. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to avoid injury.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, you should first:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Stop beside the car in front of your space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop beside the car in front of your space.
questions.explanation: After finding a space and checking traffic, stop your car parallel to the vehicle in front of your desired space. Then turn your wheels and park.

questions.question: You do not have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights if it is on a private road.
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and a stop arm extended. This rule applies on both public and private roads.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn drivers about construction, maintenance, and emergency work.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks. Always obey signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.

questions.question: Mixing drugs with alcohol:

options.text: Increases the risk of a crash.
Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
Reduces the effect of alcohol on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can damage brain function and impair driving. Combining alcohol with other drugs greatly increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, you must account for:

options.text: The longer distance needed for large vehicles to stop.
The shorter distance needed for large vehicles to stop.
The quieter noise of large vehicles.
The higher speed of large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer distance needed for large vehicles to stop.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop. Stay in positions where the truck driver can see you and where your view is not blocked by the truck.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns of low clearance ahead.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview and side mirrors before changing lanes. Also look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: What types of drugs can affect your driving?
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medications. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: Alcohol is the leading cause of fatal car crashes.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is the number one killer on American roads. It affects vision and slows reaction time. Even small amounts of alcohol can impair driving, even below the legal limit.

questions.question: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 and older, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is illegal. Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend up to 200 feet behind them.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have blind spots that extend up to 200 feet behind them. Do not follow closely behind large vehicles. The driver cannot see you there.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: In fog, you should use high beam headlights to see better.
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, use low beam headlights or fog lights. Do not use high beams in fog.

questions.question: When can you drive in a High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lane?

options.text: When you are driving faster than other traffic.
When you are driving slower than other traffic.
When your vehicle has multiple people in it.
When you are in a hurry.

questions.correctAnswerText: When your vehicle has multiple people in it.
questions.explanation: Some highways have HOV lanes for vehicles with multiple occupants. These lanes are marked with signs and diamond symbols on the road.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to stop at a railroad crossing.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights or gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices tell you to stop. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: Driving faster is the best way to avoid losing control on wet roads.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, your tires can ride up on water and cause you to lose control. This is called hydroplaning. Slow down when driving on wet roads to prevent this.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can cause death."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can cause death."
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival is unlikely. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may take risky actions to pass you.

questions.question: You cannot cross a single broken white or yellow line:

options.text: If it would interfere with other traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you has broken down.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: If it would interfere with other traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely and without interfering with other traffic.

questions.question: The most important thing about managing speed in curves is:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's inertia makes it hard to turn in curves. You must slow down before entering a curve to stay in control.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, when should you signal?

options.text: Early enough so other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Signal early when passing so other drivers have time to know your plans.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must do. It means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, flaggers, or train horns. Never try to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. Once the vehicle straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk at the bicyclist to let them know you're trying to pass.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you get a chance to pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Rush ahead to pull in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists as much space as you can. Bicyclists have less protection than drivers. Passing too quickly can push them off course.

questions.question: If traffic is backing up behind you because you're driving slowly, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Not let the other cars pass your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, you must pull off and let other vehicles pass. Only drive below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: When can you continue carefully through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: There is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane.
You are already within the intersection when the light changes to yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already within the intersection when the light changes to yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the yellow light appears, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: What does a good defensive driver do?

options.text: Looks out for the actions of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Looks out for the actions of other drivers.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver watches what other drivers are doing and expects problems. This helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: You're waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and can't see all the lanes. What should you do?

options.text: Accelerate rapidly when the first lane you need to cross is clear.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across the intersection.
Edge your car into each lane of opposing traffic as soon as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and it is safe to turn.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level greater than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving will be worse. You cannot drink and drive safely.

questions.question: When should you drive slower than the posted speed limit?

options.text: When driving on a winding road

questions.explanation: Drive at a speed that is safe for the conditions. Consider weather, visibility, road surface, road type, and traffic. Reduce your speed when conditions are unusual.

questions.question: When you see a yield sign, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.
Stop completely, even if no other cars or people are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Let pedestrians and other traffic go first. Stop if needed. If it is safe, you can go without stopping.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive with caution.

questions.question: Never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers.
questions.explanation: Never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers. It is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You can turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears, unless a sign says otherwise.

questions.question: This sign warns you that ahead is:
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a T intersection is ahead.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Does not change your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee will not lower your blood alcohol level. It may keep you awake, but it cannot make you sober or change how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.question: You must yield to children playing in the street.
questions.explanation: You must drive carefully where children are. Slow down near schools, playgrounds, and residential areas.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means you should:

options.text: Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and go when the way is clear.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "be careful." Slow down, look both ways, and proceed with caution.

questions.question: A green arrow with a red light means:

options.text: You can only drive in the direction of the arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only drive in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction the arrow points, if the intersection is clear.
